meta.titre: Vegetables and Salads: Classes, Cooking Care and Making a Good Salad
meta.sous_theme: Classes of vegetables, care of vitamins and salad making

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: At a market stall in Yaounde, a trader arranges cabbages, carrots, tomatoes, onions and garden eggs, each in its own heap. A cook who knows which class each vegetable belongs to, and how to treat it, keeps its colour, taste and vitamins. A fresh salad then turns a plain plate of rice or fish into a balanced meal. The GCE asks you to classify vegetables with examples, to explain how to cook them well, and to say why salads matter in a menu.

items: Vitamin C and the B vitamins dissolve in water.
Fibre (roughage) helps food to move through the gut.
Raw food must be washed in clean water before it is eaten.

sections.titre: Vegetables and salads: classes, care in cooking and making a salad
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Classes of vegetables
| Class | Part eaten | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Leaves | leaves | cabbage, lettuce, spinach |
| Roots | swollen root | carrot, beetroot, radish |
| Tubers | swollen underground stem | potato, yam |
| Bulbs | swollen leaf bases | onion, garlic |
| Stems | stalk | celery, asparagus |
| Flowers | flower head | cauliflower, broccoli |
| Fruits | fruit | tomato, cucumber, pepper, garden egg |
| Pods and seeds | pods or seeds | peas, green beans, sweetcorn |

Vegetables give vitamins (especially vitamin C and carotene), mineral salts such as iron, fibre and water. Most are low in fat; peas and beans also give protein, and tubers give starch.

### Preparing and cooking vegetables
- Choose fresh, firm vegetables with a good colour; prepare them just before cooking.
- Wash well, peel thinly (many vitamins lie just under the skin) and do not soak them or cut them too small.
- Cook in a little water for the shortest time, with the lid on, or steam them. Vitamin C is lost in water, by heat and by contact with air.
- Do not add bicarbonate of soda: it keeps the green colour but destroys vitamin C and makes the vegetable soft.
- Use the cooking water in soups or sauces, and serve at once.

### Salads
A salad is made of raw (or cooked and cooled) vegetables or fruit, usually served cold with a dressing. It gives freshness, colour and crispness, and its raw vegetables keep their vitamin C. Salads can be a starter, a side dish or a main course when eggs, fish, meat or beans are added. A simple dressing is oil and vinegar with seasoning; mayonnaise is made with egg yolk, oil and vinegar.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to classify vegetables and give an example of each class.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write the class, then the example, in pairs: for instance "Roots: carrot". Count the classes asked for (five classes means five pairs). Do not classify by colour or price; classify by the part of the plant that is eaten.

variantes.nom: Importance of salad in a menu
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the importance or uses of salads.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write separate points: it adds colour and an attractive look to the meal; it adds crispness and variety of texture; it adds a fresh flavour; it provides vitamins, mineral salts and fibre; it can be a light starter, a side dish or a main course; it makes a heavy meal more balanced and is easy and cheap to prepare in season.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how to prepare or serve a salad.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use fresh, crisp ingredients; wash them well and drain them dry; tear or cut them neatly; mix contrasting colours; keep the salad cold; add the dressing just before serving so that the leaves stay crisp; serve in a clean dish and garnish.

sections.enonce_markdown: Outline the steps in preparing a green salad for a family meal, and explain why the dressing is added only just before serving. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Outline" asks for the main steps in order and "explain" asks for a reason. Six marks suggest five steps and one reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part 1: steps in order. Part 2: one clear reason.

etapes.action: Start with the choice and cleaning of the ingredients.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Choose fresh, crisp lettuce and other salad vegetables. Wash them well in clean water and drain them dry.

etapes.justification: Neat preparation makes the salad attractive.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Tear the leaves or cut the vegetables into neat pieces, and arrange them in a clean, cold dish with contrasting colours.

etapes.justification: The dressing and garnish come last.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Garnish with slices of tomato or cucumber and keep the salad cold. Add the dressing just before serving.

etapes.action: Explain the timing of the dressing.
etapes.justification: A reason needs a cause and an effect.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The vinegar and salt in the dressing soften the leaves and draw water out of them, so they turn limp and soggy if the dressing is added too early.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Steps:** choose fresh crisp ingredients, wash and drain them, tear or cut neatly, arrange with contrasting colours in a clean cold dish, garnish, then add the dressing. **Reason:** the dressing is added last because its vinegar and salt soften the leaves and draw out water, so the salad would lose its crispness.

items.erreur_markdown: Classifying vegetables as "red, green and yellow" or as "cheap and costly".
items.pourquoi_faux: Vegetables are classified by the part of the plant that is eaten.
items.correction_markdown: Use the classes leaves, roots, tubers, bulbs, stems, flowers, fruits, and pods and seeds, with one example each.

items.erreur_markdown: Putting a tomato under "roots" and a carrot under "fruits".
items.pourquoi_faux: A tomato is the fruit of the plant and a carrot is a swollen root.
items.correction_markdown: Tomato: fruit vegetable. Carrot: root vegetable.

items.erreur_markdown: Boiling cabbage for a long time in plenty of water, with bicarbonate of soda, to make it soft and green.
items.pourquoi_faux: Vitamin C dissolves in water, is destroyed by heat and air, and is destroyed by bicarbonate of soda. A long boil also spoils the colour and flavour.
items.correction_markdown: Shred it just before cooking, cook in a little boiling water with the lid on for a short time, and use the water.

items.erreur_markdown: Mixing the dressing into the salad an hour before the guests arrive so that it will "soak in".
items.pourquoi_faux: The vinegar and salt make the leaves limp and watery.
items.correction_markdown: Keep the dressing apart and add it at the last moment.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing "salad is cheap" as the only importance of salad in a menu.
items.pourquoi_faux: One cost point does not earn five marks and it is not always true.
items.correction_markdown: Give separate points on colour, texture, flavour, vitamins and fibre, and variety.

items.enonce_markdown: State the class of vegetable (leaf, root, bulb, flower, fruit, or pod and seed) to which each of these belongs: carrot, spinach, cauliflower, onion, tomato, peas.
items.solution_markdown: Carrot: **root**. Spinach: **leaf**. Cauliflower: **flower**. Onion: **bulb**. Tomato: **fruit**. Peas: **pod and seed**.

items.enonce_markdown: A cook buys the ingredients of a mixed salad for 8 people: lettuce $400$ FCFA, tomatoes $600$ FCFA, cucumber $300$ FCFA, carrots $250$ FCFA, and oil and vinegar for the dressing $450$ FCFA. (a) Find the total cost. (b) Find the cost per person. (c) The cook adds $500$ FCFA of extra vegetables to serve 10 people. Find the new cost per person.

A canteen cook chops cabbage finely, soaks it in water for an hour, boils it for 40 minutes in a large pot with bicarbonate of soda, and throws the water away. (a) Name the vitamin that is mainly lost. (b) Give four faults in this method. (c) Describe a better way to cook the cabbage.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Vitamin C.** (b) Any four of: chopping it too finely; soaking it for a long time (the vitamin dissolves in the water); using a large amount of water; boiling for too long; adding bicarbonate of soda (it destroys vitamin C); throwing away the cooking water, which holds the vitamins and mineral salts. (c) Wash the cabbage and shred it just before cooking, put it into a little boiling water, cover with a lid and cook for a short time until just tender (or steam it), then serve at once and keep the water for soup or sauce.

items_markdown: Vegetables are classed by the part eaten: leaves, roots, tubers, bulbs, stems, flowers, fruits, and pods and seeds; learn one example for each.
Vegetables supply vitamins, mineral salts, fibre and water; peas and beans also supply protein.
Protect vitamin C: prepare late, peel thinly, use little water, a short time, a lid, no bicarbonate of soda, and use the cooking water.
A salad is served cold with a dressing; it adds colour, crispness, flavour, vitamins and fibre, and can be a starter, side dish or main course.
Wash and drain salad ingredients, keep them cold, and add the dressing at the last moment.
When a question asks for a number of points, write that number of separate points.
